title: Akeega and prednisolone: BRCA-selected prostate treatment
indication_text: BRCA1/2-mutated metastatic castration-resistant prostate cancer when chemotherapy is not clinically indicated.
purpose: Delay progression in BRCA1/2-mutated metastatic castration-resistant prostate cancer when chemotherapy is not clinically indicated. This treatment aims to control advanced cancer.
schedule_label: Daily tablets plus prescribed steroid and ADT
schedule_summary: Usual starting dose: two Akeega 100/500 mg tablets once daily, plus prednisolone 10 mg daily. Continue your hormone injections unless you have had surgical castration. Treatment is continuous, with no routine rest week.
administration_text: Take Akeega whole with water at least two hours after food, then wait at least one hour before eating. Take prednisolone with food. If a dose is missed, take it as soon as possible on the same day; do not take extra tablets. Check with the team after vomiting. The two Akeega strengths are not interchangeable.
monitoring_summary: Blood count: weekly in month 1, fortnightly in months 2-3, then monthly to year 1 and every two months thereafter. Liver tests: fortnightly for months 1-3, then monthly to year 1 and every two months thereafter. Blood pressure: weekly for two months, then monthly to year 1 and every two months thereafter. Potassium: monthly to year 1, then every two months.

agents.name: Niraparib (in Akeega)
agents.mechanism: Blocks PARP-dependent DNA repair, exploiting the cancer’s BRCA-related repair weakness.
agents.explanation: Blocks PARP-dependent DNA repair, exploiting the cancer’s BRCA-related repair weakness.
agents.watch: Report fever, infection, unusual bleeding, breathlessness or severe headache promptly.
risks: Low red cells (anaemia), low platelets and infection risk from low white cells
Nausea, vomiting, constipation, fatigue and poor appetite
High blood pressure, dizziness or headache
Rare bone-marrow cancers (MDS/AML); rare severe neurological syndrome (PRES)

agents.name: Abiraterone (in Akeega)
agents.mechanism: Blocks CYP17 to reduce androgen production; this can also increase mineralocorticoid effects.
agents.explanation: Blocks CYP17 to reduce androgen production; this can also increase mineralocorticoid effects.
agents.watch: Keep blood pressure, potassium and liver-test checks.
risks: High blood pressure, fluid retention and low potassium
Liver injury, occasionally severe or fatal
Heart failure, rhythm changes, clots or chest pain
Muscle symptoms, bone loss and fractures

agents.name: Prednisolone
agents.mechanism: Suppresses ACTH drive to limit abiraterone-related mineralocorticoid excess.
agents.explanation: Suppresses ACTH drive to limit abiraterone-related mineralocorticoid excess.
agents.watch: Take the prescribed steroid with food; do not stop suddenly.
risks: Raised glucose, appetite or sleep and mood changes
Infection risk, stomach irritation and bone effects
Adrenal insufficiency if withdrawn suddenly or during illness

chronology_notes.title: Safety and practical points
chronology_notes.text: Do not stop prednisolone suddenly, including when Akeega is held. Ask about steroid cover during illness. Dose reductions differ for low blood counts and liver injury; always follow the exact tablet strength and number on the revised prescription. Use condoms with a pregnant partner, or condoms plus another effective method with a partner who could become pregnant, during treatment and for four months after the last dose.

items.title: Your treatment setting
items.text: BRCA1/2-mutated metastatic castration-resistant prostate cancer when chemotherapy is not clinically indicated.

items.title: How it works
items.text: Niraparib inhibits PARP proteins used in DNA repair. BRCA-altered cancer already has a weakness in another repair pathway, making this additional block more damaging to cancer cells. Abiraterone reduces androgen production by blocking CYP17. Prednisolone limits the hormone imbalance caused by that block.

Radiotherapy may still have a role for symptoms or another agreed local treatment goal.

evidence.title: What the evidence can tell you
evidence.intro: Trial results describe groups of people; they cannot predict an individual outcome.
evidence.population: MAGNITUDE BRCA1/2 subgroup: 225 participants with first-line mCRPC; 113 assigned niraparib plus abiraterone/steroid.
evidence.comparison: Niraparib + abiraterone/prednisone versus placebo + abiraterone/prednisone; ADT maintained.
evidence.interpretation: At the primary analysis, median time without scan progression or death was 16.6 versus 10.9 months; hazard ratio 0.533 (95% CI 0.361-0.789). Final overall-survival HR was 0.788 (95% CI 0.554-1.120), which did not establish an overall-survival advantage. The progression and survival analyses used different data cut-offs. These figures are not an individual prediction.
limitations: BRCA subgroup and mCRPC setting; do not extend these figures to all prostate cancers.
Radiographic progression-free survival is not overall survival.
Primary progression analysis: October 2021 cut-off; final survival: May 2023 cut-off. EMA SmPC section 5.1, Table 6.
